title: KernelSyscallCoverageMatrix
description: Canonical single-source-of-truth (SSOT) tracker for the framekernel's full-Linux-syscall-ABI program (ADR-0009 operational note #2). A per-architecture matrix of EVERY Linux syscall number on each SUPPORTED arch (aarch64/arm64 + x86_64; riscv64 is a noted LATER third backend), each row recording implementation status, owning subsystem, differential-oracle verification, the demand signal that pulled it (or that it is still unmet), and notes. Status per row: 'implemented' (real semantics), 'stub' (present in dispatch, fixed/no-op return), or 'enosys' (unimplemented; the -ENOSYS catch-all is itself the demand signal). This file is source-shaped and machine-generated from specs/_gen_matrix.py against the live dispatch tables in cloud/cloud-kernel/crates/arch-{x86_64,aarch64}/src/user.rs. Honest non-claim: 'implemented'/'differential_verified' describe the CURRENT demand-driven talos-init+svc boot set; the FULL ABI is the committed TARGET reached incrementally, never an all-at-once claim.

_meta.purpose: Authoritative per-arch syscall coverage tracker for the complete-Linux-ABI program: enumerate every syscall number on each supported arch, mark implemented/stub/enosys, record differential-oracle verification and the demand signal, and surface per-arch summary counts so coverage growth is evidence-backed and demand-prioritised (never speculative).

arch_notes.aarch64: arm64 generic asm-generic unistd ABI (__NR_*), ~295 numbered syscalls. The modern at-suffixed forms only (openat, not open; mkdirat, not mkdir; ppoll, not poll; clone, not fork).
arch_notes.x86_64: arch/x86/entry/syscalls/syscall_64.tbl 64-bit ABI, ~350 active numbers plus the recent tail; carries legacy non-at forms (open, dup2, mkdir, fork, poll) AND arch_prctl. x32-only entries are excluded.
arch_notes.riscv64: LATER third Frame backend; shares the asm-generic unistd table with aarch64 (~295). Not enumerated here until the K4->K7 bring-up ladder reaches it; the full ABI is completed first on aarch64 + x86_64 (ADR-0009 operational note #3).

methodology.summary: Differential-tested incremental coverage toward the COMPLETE Linux syscall ABI on the two supported arches; never a single big-bang implementation (ADR-0009, alternative C accepted).
methodology.diff_oracle_is_the_spine: Run the same unmodified static Linux binary on real Linux vs our kernel; diff the normalized syscall trace. A -ENOSYS return (or a behavioural divergence) is the DEMAND SIGNAL for the next syscall. Coverage is demand-prioritised, not speculative.
methodology.enosys_is_the_demand_signal: The dispatcher's -ENOSYS catch-all is load-bearing: every 'enosys' row in this matrix is an explicit next-candidate. demand_source on those rows reads 'unmet (-ENOSYS demand signal)'.
methodology.per_syscall_gate: Each syscall lands via the established bounded implement -> INDEPENDENT adversarial-verify cycle, gated on: build-both (aarch64 + x86_64) + boot-both + golden byte-identical trace + check-tcb (safe-kernel 0-unsafe). Coverage grows WITHOUT TCB regression: syscalls dispatch into the #![forbid(unsafe_code)] safe kernel; arch glue stays in the audited Frame.
methodology.conformance_bar: Pass the Linux Test Project (LTP) syscall suite AND run arbitrary unmodified musl/glibc static binaries. 'We support Linux' is never claimed before the LTP suite actually passes (ADR-0009).
methodology.differential_verified_semantics: differential_verified=true ONLY where a golden / diff-oracle trace currently covers the syscall on that arch; default false. It is a coverage fact, not an aspiration.

status_legend.implemented: Real Linux semantics (struct layouts, flags, errno) implemented and dispatched.
status_legend.stub: Present in dispatch but returns a fixed / no-op value (e.g., fcntl->0, lseek->-ESPIPE, ioctl->-ENOTTY, munmap/mprotect no-op, futex->0).
status_legend.enosys: Unimplemented; falls through the dispatcher's -ENOSYS catch-all. This return is the demand signal for prioritising the syscall.

generation.regeneration: Re-run the generator to refresh; this JSON is the committed SSOT artifact and must stay in sync with the dispatch tables.

summary.note: Counts are over every numbered syscall on each arch. implemented+stub is the current demand-driven boot set (talos-init 7-phase sequencer + svc to clean power-off, M1/M2 verified); the remainder are enosys (the full-ABI target). riscv64 is not yet enumerated (later backend).
